questions.q: Do the potato osmosis practical at home (0%, 5%, 10% salt) with an adult, or use the class data. (a) Calculate % changes [2]. (b) Plot % change against concentration [2]. (c) Estimate the concentration with no net change and explain [3].
questions.a: (a) e.g. +8%, -6%, -15% (2); (b) correct axes and line (2); (c) where the line crosses 0%, about 3% (1); no net movement of water (1) because the solution has the same water concentration as the cells (1)
questions.model: Teacher calculates the first % change on screen.

questions.q: Explain why root hair cells need active transport for mineral ions.
questions.a: Ions are at a lower concentration in the soil than in the cell (1); moving them against the gradient needs energy from respiration (1)

questions.q: A piece goes from 1.80 g to 1.98 g. % change?
Why calculate % change instead of change in mass?
questions.a: Pieces start at different masses, so % allows fair comparison
Net movement of water (1) across a partially permeable membrane (1) from dilute to more concentrated solution (1)
